means: The main context line of a session; during a stem it holds only the stem's handle and step lines.
A branch (git plus context) taken at the goal's turn; work runs there and folds back to the core line.
The turn where a stem branches; a cache checkpoint can sit there (stem anchor).
The stem's result re-pointed into the core line's handle once the stem finishes.
An opaque id whose bytes stay fixed in the cached prefix while what it resolves to changes.
Change what a handle resolves to in the store without editing the context bytes.
Read what a handle currently holds, with the read tool the model already uses.
Model asks for what it needs by handle, instead of the harness pushing a narrative.
A cache breakpoint chosen where it pays: system, tail or stem anchor kind.
A named versioned spec the turn loop reads at fixed seams, id strat-<name>-<major>.<minor>.
A module boundary where behavior plugs in: tools, providers, strategies, hooks, policies, handles, checkpoints, machine, coord.
A small model that checks each completed tool call and answers ok or FLAG with a reason.
A watcher note on a tool call, stored on the session (s.flags) and counted as a smell.
An operator's assessment of a session against its goal, stored as s.watched.
A Claude Code session that drives harness sessions through scripts/wh.mjs and reports what it cannot resolve.
A point before each model request or tool call where a session can be held.
State of a session waiting at a gate until step or resume.
One lockstep advance: every waiting session takes one step and holds again.
Stop every tab at its next gate; used for lockstep and for updates.
A turn spent to inspect a wait point; a passing check needs no wake.
Re-pointing what handles resolve to so a stem's downstream turns see altered or materialized context.
Write real turn content into the context where a handle stood.
The component that decides what a handle resolves to; the micro resolver is a small model doing so at the leading edge.
Models consult at checkpoints: A ahead, B look-back, plus a consult; arranged as a graph.
A generic prompt turn with a throwaway reply that registers the cache for a byte-stable payload.
A tracked issue (labels concern, kind:*, ci-failure, triaged, needs-*) worked in the background loop.
A recorded oddity (wh:smells: kind, tool, detail, steer fingerprint) tracked over time.
The generic points and directions given to a session; logged in the log repo.
Per-turn session rows: prompt, cached, cacheWrite, completion, reasoning, cost, bp kinds, strat id, upstream.
A live value drawn by CSS from data-v via slot(el, value); changes without re-rendering.
A named CSS rule via rule(name, css); UI state is a rule, not a node edit.
Checks written from the goal and committed red before the implementation.
A check fails (red) before implementation and passes (green) after.
A measured comparison against plain serial turns, run with scripts/casestudy.mjs.
The baseline: plain serial turns without stems; results are reported relative to it.
The provider route behind a model on OpenRouter; stems inherit the core's upstream so the cache holds.
The shared in-browser VM and its host, with per-session unix users.
A set of sessions sharing a profile (settings such as strategy and watchModel).
A redaction handle form: what it resolves to is hidden from the model.
A registered function on the terminal path, direction up or down, that sanitizes or alters text; register(dir, name, label, fn).
A rule in app/policy.js that decides whether a tool call or write is allowed or needs approval.
Text cut short on screen that shows whole on hover or press-and-hold, from data-full or a slot's data-v.
A segmented page element built once by item() or R.part(); segments are filled, the card is never rebuilt.
Render rule: a node is created once and never rebuilt; state shows through slots and rules.
The in-page dialog modal({title, body, actions}) that replaces alert, confirm and prompt.
An edit panel on a row with discard, keep editing or save, shown from and to values.
How a model steers its own work unaided; observed before any structure is added.
Fixing a workflow as explicit steps in the prompt, compared against natural steering and altered or materialized turns.
A second model, given procedures and background, swaps or alters turns or the flow of the first model's session.
A strategy that applies only where a condition holds, such as a long core; its own id, compared with serial.
A real development session driven as a person drives it through scripts/wh.mjs; never a puzzle or challenge prompt.
The test-only provider with a modelled prefix cache; proves mechanics, not model behaviour.
A per-agent append-only file catalog/inbox/<agent>-<shortid>.jsonl that only the steward merges into the catalog.
The eight steps every piece of work follows, from naming it to release, with fixed owners.
After a group of turns, send the context plus a marker, ask for one word, discard the reply; the product is a cache entry.
Markers like [label, tag, tag] in the cached prefix that later resolvers give meaning to, instead of a concrete steer baked into cached bytes.
A judged payload of past turns plus an instruction naming the action; the model commits to one line; dropped after a few light turns.
A small model builds a payload from data, not content (under 10k tokens); a frontier model then operates on it.
Helper work is capped by max_tokens, a payload budget and a ledger row per operation, with a smell over the cap.
One harness-added request: watch, helper, steward, probe, nudge, graft, recraft or confer; cost taken from its ledger row.
A helper rewrites one wordy reasoning block, dropping loops and never renaming a name; the raw text stays in the log behind a handle.
Named voices with structure, before/after and degree of coherence, chosen by strategy policy.
Marking terms as crafted, proper, label or regular: a deterministic first pass, then a zero-shot pass that only proposes.
One per-instance markdown file read by helper workers as a cached prefix; workers carry no context between items.
One experiment's two arms, blue (current plus exact brief) and green (candidate), each with its own session, strategy id and throwaway branch.
The first silo stage: one task, one run per arm, hard cost cap; stop if green costs over 2x blue or is unreviewable.
A Fable subagent run in Claude Code, not the API, that proposes falsifiable hypotheses and never touches a branch.
The manual baseline: name files and lines, copy find strings from what was just read, one file per commit, stop at the approval card.
Steering that comes from the strategy (system-prompt base plus hooked turn wrappers), versioned with the strategy id; a hand nudge is a missing directive.
Any wh say after the first message that is not an approval answer; counted from the wh log, target 0 for green.
Tool results byte-identical to an earlier result of the same tool in the session, over all tool calls.
Metadata-only profile of every session's turns, with a drill by index into content only where a number points; descriptive, never a verdict.
Dark, light and system modes as named CSS custom properties that developers can override.
Cost, tokens, cache, calls and checkpoints as widgets the user places in named slots; developers register widgets.
Per-part templates and an ordered text-transform pipeline with sanitized inline markup, so turn appearance is open to developers.
A stored, ordered sequence of turns (a conversation track) from a catalog; applied at bootstrap or mid-session.
The set of flows plus the approaches that allocate their turns, with what each policy, trigger and resolution aimed for.
A cheap helper model that picks which flow starts or joins a conversation, before any provider API is called.
An attributable label on a turn or flow, kept beside the turns; means anything; tags and flows are many-to-many.
A change of a conversation's tag set along the way; the first set is the tag pivot.
A rule binding a tag set to a flow with a trigger, an aim and a per-strategy awareness setting.
A turn with typed fields (voice, content, context values) and a validation shape, holding no fixed wording.
The typed parameters of a turn template; not a UI slot (see slot).
An advanced pre-allocated stack of templated turns, filled by helpers, heuristics or both.
Like a turn stack but dispersed through the conversation, allocation guaranteed by policy.
A check extracted from one step bullet or directive of a skill or agent md file, run as a flow's turns resolve steps.
Analytics over tags, flows, validations and costs that assess the flow approach itself: quality gained and tokens saved against baselines.
Cheap helper or logic that picks a flow per case against a route rubric, pre-provider, any provider; records confidence per pick.
Pre-allocated templated turns, e.g. spun up to meet a provider cache size floor before the flow is sent.
Templated turns dispersed through the conversation, allocation guaranteed by policy; saturated dithering is so dense it looks serial.
A check from one step bullet of a skill or agent md file; never blocks, it carries issues and tags to flows.
Timestamped, session and flow-state attributed data, never rewritten, queried to find successes, issues and further strategies.
The labels and directive saying when a flow should be routed a given way; the router is judged against it.
The stated starting basis of a tag set; easy to gauge, record and verify beside the turns.
Where tags are made and documented in flight, then asserted after the fact.
A trial of a pitched tag with its hypothesis, using all existing conventions, before the flow relies on it.
Changing a flow's protocol mid-flow when it shows more issues than anticipated; the flow then continues.
One tagged policy's thread through the chronological turn state; strands pick up and fall off interleaved.
The strands of all active tagged policies together, across flows.
Resolves what falls outside the scope of the tagged policies so the strand meets back into scope.
One policy tag's run along the turn state; strides of several policies pass each other.
Turn dithering so dense that the conversation looks serial.
A terse cached context a hot agent works from.
An active agent that produces or guides turns from baked templates off a context pin.
A small API call tapped against a hot agent's delegator state; many do much of the heavy lifting.
A policy seam's parameters and its return payload shape.
